The draft answers Nessa's question with a clear, honest no and explains why: she shouldn't make up the missed runs after a fever. The week eases her back in. Monday is a walk only, there are two short walk-runs instead of three, rest days sit between them, and Wednesday only goes ahead if the cough is settling. That fits a beginner who had a fever until Friday and still has a cough, and the volume stays at or below her recent 7 km weeks. So I don't see a breach of the illness, returning-runner or volume checks.

Why it's not a 5:
- "Wiped out" is only covered by the fever reasoning. The draft never names the tiredness or tells her to sleep more or back off further if she still feels drained.
- Saturday has no symptom check, so she might run it even if the cough is no better.
- There's no advice to see a doctor if the cough lingers or her chest gets worse.
- It doesn't mention the 15 November 5K, so she gets no reassurance about whether her goal is still on track.

── NESSA'S WEEK ──
Nessa is 41 and new to running, aiming to run the whole Corrowmore Harvest 5K on 15 November without walking. Nessa walk-runs three mornings a week (Monday, Wednesday and Saturday) and walks the dog most days.
Recent weeks: 6.8, 7.3 km
This week: 2.8 km over 1 run. Missed 2 of 3 planned runs.
Body: "Came down with a cold on Tuesday that turned into a fever, 38.4 on Wednesday night. No fever since Friday but still coughing and blocked up."
Feeling: "Wiped out."
Asks: "Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Nessa: You are coming off a fever and still coughing, so next week eases back in rather than making up what you missed. …
Answers: No, please do not do that. Two rules after a fever: wait until you have been fever-free for a few days before running again (you have), and do not try to replace missed sessions, because the body is still recovering even once the temperature is normal.
Safety flag: Returning after a fever
Next week:
Mon: easy, 25 min brisk walk, no running, just see how your chest and legs feel moving…
Tue: rest. Recovery day while you are still shaking off the cold.
Wed: easy, 20 min walk-run, 6 x 2 min run and 1 min walk, only if the cough is settling…
Thu: rest. Keeps the running days spaced while you recover.
Fri: rest. Protects Saturday's longer session.
Sat: easy, 24 min walk-run, 8 x 2 min run and 1 min walk, same effort as early…
Sun: rest. Full day off to close the week.
